chapter_metadata.title: Electrocautery and Argon Plasma Coagulation
chapter_metadata.reference: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology, 2025

definitions.definition: Direct-contact thermal ablation using high-frequency electrical current to cut and coagulate airway tissue.
Non-contact monopolar electrocoagulation via ionized argon plasma that causes superficial coagulation (~1–2 mm).
Obstruction of trachea and main bronchi from benign or malignant disease leading to airflow limitation.
Continuous radial expansion balloon used for airway dilation after web or stenosis incisions.

technology_and_technique.summary: High-frequency current delivered through an insulated wire probe; heat generated at the point of contact from electron current density; requires grounding pad to complete circuit and protect operator.

Argon gas ionized at probe tip forms plasma jet; electrons spray to closest tissue, creating homogeneous superficial coagulative necrosis (~1–2 mm). Plasma can follow bronchial angulations; aim so target is closest surface.
Dependent on wattage, probe size (smaller tip concentrates energy), and activation duration. Mucus/blood/metal can shunt current and diminish local effect; clear the field with suction.
Yellow pedal: cutting; blue pedal: coagulation. EC blend mode alternates voltages for simultaneous cutting/coagulation. Alternate pedals as needed.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pre-procedure radiographic assessment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Define lesion location, depth suspicion, and distal lumen presence to select modality (EC vs APC vs laser) and plan multimodal therapy.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: APC favored for superficial coagulation/hemostasis or uncertain depth; EC/laser more efficient for bulk debulking when distal lumen present.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Endoscopic lesion assessment
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Characterize endoluminal vs extrinsic compression and bleeding propensity.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Endoluminal disease → EC/APC appropriate; extrinsic compression alone → not an indication for EC/APC; mixed disease → consider ablation + dilation/stent.

clinical_procedures.name: Needle knife radial incisions for webs/stenosis
steps: Position needle-knife at 12 o'clock; short activation to incise superficially.
Repeat at 3 and 9 o'clock (and additional quadrants if needed).
Avoid posterior membranous wall to prevent esophageal injury.
Follow with CRE balloon dilation until adequate lumen achieved.
post_steps: Assess for bleeding and stabilize eschar

clinical_procedures.name: Snare excision for pedunculated tumors
indications: Pedunculated endobronchial tumors with visible stalk
steps: Loop snare at stalk base; tighten to compress blood supply.
Apply EC in brief bursts while tightening until release.
Retrieve specimen with forceps; treat base for hemostasis.
pitfalls: Prolonged activation leading to deep thermal injury

clinical_procedures.name: Hot forceps biopsy (limited role)
indications: When concurrent coagulation during biopsy is desired
clinical_procedures.notes: Evidence has not shown significant bleeding reduction vs cold forceps; rarely used in current practice.

clinical_procedures.name: Blunt probe cauterization
steps: Apply probe tip to target tissue; short activations with suction.
Reassess tissue effect frequently; avoid long activations.

clinical_procedures.name: APC non-contact coagulation
indications: When depth is uncertain or distal lumen absent
steps: Advance probe ~2 cm distal to scope tip and keep visible.
Aim 1–3 mm from target; short bursts with painting motion.
Coagulate layer-by-layer to achieve devitalized eschar; then mechanically debulk if needed.
safety: Keep probe distal to scope tip

clinical_guidelines.title: Indications & contraindications
specific_recommendations: Use EC/APC for endoluminal CAO of benign/malignant etiologies.
Not indicated for pure extrinsic compression.
For mixed endoluminal + extrinsic disease, plan multimodal therapy (ablation + dilation or stenting).

clinical_guidelines.title: Perioperative safety & room preparation
specific_recommendations: Apply grounding pad; remove metallic objects.
Perform pre-activation safety check with anesthesia; confirm FiO2 <40% (or ≤3 L/min under sedation).
If FiO2 cannot be reduced safely, choose nonthermal alternatives (e.g., cryotherapy).
Manage implantable devices: pre-op evaluation; magnet for pacer-dependency; deprogram/reprogram ICDs.

clinical_guidelines.title: Parameter selection
specific_recommendations: EC: 20–60 W starting point; long duration (higher cutting), low effect (lower coagulation).
APC: 20–40 W; argon 0.3–1.8 L/min; maintain flow <1 L/min to reduce gas embolism risk.

clinical_guidelines.title: Intra-procedural monitoring
specific_recommendations: Use suction during energy delivery to maintain visualization and limit shunting from blood/mucus.
Pause for desaturations; temporarily increase FiO2, then reduce <40% before resuming.
Mechanically remove devitalized tissue (forceps or cryoprobe) after coagulation.

tables.title: Starting parameters and key technique notes for EC and APC
rows: Long duration/low effect to begin; alternate pedals; suction during activation
Probe ~2 cm beyond scope tip; layer-by-layer coagulation

tables.title: Perioperative checklist for thermal airway ablation
rows: Pacer magnet if dependent; ICD off during case and reprogram after
Smoke/char removal; clear field to avoid shunting
Cryotherapy or other if FiO2 cannot be reduced

figures.caption: Subglottic web: needle-knife radial cuts; avoid posterior membrane; CRE balloon dilation for lumen gain.
High tracheal tumor: APC circumferential devitalization then cryoprobe debulking → improved caliber and hemoptysis resolution.

management: Choose EC for efficient debulking when contact is safe and distal lumen present; choose APC for superficial coagulation/hemostasis or uncertain depth.
Combine with mechanical debulking and dilatation; consider stenting for residual narrowing or mixed disease.

points: EC and APC deliver immediate, controllable thermal ablation for endoluminal CAO with strong symptomatic and anatomic responses in selected patients.
APC’s shallow penetration favors safety in uncertain depth or absent distal lumen, while EC offers faster debulking via contact energy.
Strict FiO2 thresholds and gas-flow discipline are central to avoiding airway fire and gas embolism; structured team workflows reduce risk.
